law: Charity regulators can compel an answer from individual temples and national bodies.
money: Book distribution and temple economies are described under Money above.
reach: The 'bad association' doctrine discourages contact with critics, ex-members, and outside interpretations of the scriptures.
techniques: Thirty named techniques from domestic-abuse and social-psychology research, applied to institutions, in the eight stages of the cycle.
loops: The seven loops below show how the practices connect, so that each step makes the next one easier and the last step feeds the first.
say-do: The zonal ācārya system was dismantled and residential schooling largely ended — a genuine structural change, and rare in this codex.
cost: Leaving costs one's entire community and often years of unpaid labor with no equity.
ledger: Institutional continuity and guru positions benefit, as do the movement's assets built on devotee labor.
who-gets-hurt: The harm recorded in the earlier sections does not fall evenly.
tiers: The institution's routine work is done below the GBC, by people who apply quotas, run schools and temples, and see the consequences.
questions: A devotee gives twenty-five years of full-time labor.
